Based on my comprehensive research, I can now provide you with a detailed summary of the data and methodology for estimating Georgia's capital stock for 2000-2023.

## Summary of Findings

I've conducted extensive searches across multiple databases and sources. Here's what I found:

### **1. Available Capital Stock Data for 2015-2019**

From **FRED / Penn World Table 10.01**, Georgia's capital stock (at current PPP in millions of 2017 USD):
- 2015: ~231,600
- 2016: ~238,500  
- 2017: ~248,033
- 2018: ~254,090
- 2019: ~263,192

**Source:** [Capital stock at Current Purchasing Power Parities for Georgia (FRED)](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/CKSPPPGEA666NRUG)

### **2. Gross Capital Formation / Fixed Investment Data**

**Available sources for 2000-2023:**

| Source | Format | Coverage |
|--------|--------|----------|
| **World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.CD** | Current USD | 2000-2023 available |
| **World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.ZS** | % of GDP | 2000-2023 available |
| **CEIC Data** | USD Millions (quarterly) | 1996-2025 quarterly data |
| **Geostat (National Statistics Office of Georgia)** | Local currency | 2000-2023 |

**Access these at:**
- [World Bank Gross fixed capital formation (current US$)](https://data.worldbank.org/indicator/NE.GDI.FTOT.CD)
- [CEIC Georgia Gross Fixed Capital Formation](https://www.ceicdata.com/en/indicator/georgia/gross-fixed-capital-formation)
- [Geostat National Accounts](https://www.geostat.ge/en/modules/categories/22/national-accounts)

**Sample data points from CEIC:**
- 2023: ~1.748-1.917 USD billion (quarterly)
- Average depreciation of capital stock over the period ~0.6-0.7 billion USD annually based on quarterly trends

### **3. Depreciation Rates for Perpetual Inventory Method**

Based on **IMF and Penn World Table methodology**, for middle-income countries like Georgia:

**By Asset Type (Penn World Table 11.0 methodology):**
- Residential structures: 1.1% annual
- Non-residential structures: 3.1% annual  
- Machinery & equipment: 12.6% annual
- Transport equipment: 18.9% annual
- Computers: 31.5% annual
- Communication equipment: 11.5% annual
- Software/IP products: 15-31.5% annual

**Aggregate depreciation rate for middle-income countries:**
- **Range: 4.25% to 7% annually** (time-varying)
- **Typical assumption: 5-6% for general capital stock** (recommended for Georgia)
- Rising from ~2.5% in 1960 to 3.5% by 2001 for middle-income countries in IMF methodology

**Sources:**
- [IMF Investment and Capital Stock Dataset (ICSD) 2021](https://infrastructuregovern.imf.org/content/dam/PIMA/Knowledge-Hub/dataset/InvestmentandCapitalStockDatabaseUserManualandFAQ_May2021.pdf)
- [Penn World Table 11.0](https://www.rug.nl/ggdc/productivity/pwt/?lang=en)
- [IMF Public Investment Analysis](https://www.imf.org/external/np/fad/publicinvestment/pdf/csupdate_aug19.pdf)

### **4. Implementation Recommendations**

To fill missing years (2000-2014 and 2020-2023) using perpetual inventory method:

**Formula:** K(t) = I(t) + (1-δ)*K(t-1)

**Recommended approach:**
1. **Download World Bank NE.GDI.FTOT.CD** (current USD) for 2000-2023
2. **Deflate to constant 2017 prices** using World Bank GDP deflator
3. **Use δ = 0.05 to 0.06** (5-6% annually) for aggregate capital stock
4. **For 2000-2014:** Work backwards from 2015 capital stock using actual investment data
5. **For 2020-2023:** Continue forward using current investment data

**Key references to cite:**
- [Georgia Country Economic Memorandum - World Bank](https://documents1.worldbank.org/curated/en/099320306302241716/pdf/P1754860e2ca09010a38901096450aa920.pdf) - Shows capital formation was 8% of GDP (2012-2018) for SOEs alone
- [World Bank Data on Georgia](https://data.worldbank.org/country/georgia)
- [Geostat National Accounts Database](https://www.geostat.ge/en)

### **Data Tables Available:**

The most accessible sources to get your data in table format:
1. **World Bank DataBank** - allows CSV/Excel download for all years, multiple indicators
2. **CEIC Data** - provides quarterly data you can aggregate to annual figures
3. **Penn World Table** - direct download of capital stock series for all years 1950-2023 (latest PWT 11.0)

All these sources provide data in downloadable formats suitable for spreadsheet analysis.
